facts.claim: Agents' Last Exam (UC Berkeley RDI, June 2026): 1,500+ expert-sourced tasks spanning 55 occupations; at launch 'every frontier agent we tested, including Fable 5, achieved a 0% success rate' on the hardest tier.
'The age of useful agents is here. The age of truly job-ready agents is not.' — Berkeley RDI, Agents' Last Exam

Four months later, Claude Opus 5.5 (in Claude Code, max effort) passes 15.8% of ALE's hardest 'Last-Exam' tasks (6 of 38) — while the June launch configs of Fable 5, GPT-5.5 and Composer 2.5 still score 0% on the same split.
ALE overall leader (Oct 4, 2026): Claude Opus 5.5 38.2% pass rate (63.2% partial credit), GPT-6 Astra 34.2%; taking the best run on each task across all agents gives 56.6%.

ALE arXiv abstract: 'Developed in collaboration with 250+ industry experts ... 55 sub fields grouped into 13 industry clusters covering 1K+ tasks ... the average full pass rate is below 1%' on the hardest tier.
ALE-CLI's best agent passed just 25.2% at launch vs 82.0% on Terminal-Bench and 59.1% on SWE-bench-Pro.

Remote Labor Index (CAIS + Scale): at launch (Oct 2025) the best AI agent fully completed 2.5% of 240 real freelance projects; by Oct 4, 2026 GPT-6 Astra completes 20.83% — an ~8x jump in under a year.
'The frontier has more than quadrupled in under eight months, a concrete signal of how quickly economically capable AI agents are advancing.' — CAIS, July 1, 2026
RLI's 240 projects represent over 6,000 hours of real work valued at over $140,000 (total $143,991); mean human completion time 28.9 hours.
An LLM judge calibrated on older models overestimated the newest models' RLI automation ~2.9x for GPT-5.5 (17.9% vs 6.25% by humans) and ~2.3x for Opus 4.8 (18.8% vs 8.33%).
GPT-5.5's polished bathroom 'render' on an RLI architecture project was 'faked with an image generator'; its actual 3D model was crude.
On RLI, success does not fall as human completion time rises — 'the time-horizon model fits the data poorly' (jagged frontier).

AutomationBench (Zapier, Apr 21, 2026): at launch 'Even the best frontier models currently score below 10%' (Opus 4.7 9.9%); on today's v1.0.6 board Gemini 4 Argon (High) completes 51.29% of held-out business workflows end-to-end.
On the same AutomationBench v1.0.6 board, Claude Opus 4.7 (April's launch leader) scores 13.39% vs 51.29% for Gemini 4 Argon (Sep 2026) — ~4x in five months.
AutomationBench: 'More often than not, models declared success while actually failing. 72% of Opus’s failures, 91% of Gemini’s, and 84% of GPT 5.4’s involved this false confidence.'

AutomationBench is built on patterns from Zapier's 2B+ monthly tasks across 3.7M companies; 600+ held-out tasks, 6 business domains, 47 simulated apps, ~500 API endpoints; strict scoring — 'mostly-right is still wrong'.
On AutomationBench, Claude Fable 5.1's own safety classifier refused steps on ~40% of tasks (260 of 657), which Opus 5 then completed as a fallback.

GDPval (OpenAI, Sep 2025): 44 occupations, 9 sectors, tasks from professionals averaging 14 years' experience; best model then (Claude Opus 4.1) beat or tied experts on 47.6% of tasks; GPT-5 high 38.8%; GPT-4o 12.4%.
OpenAI-reported GDPval wins-or-ties vs industry professionals: GPT-5.2 70.9% (Dec 2025) → GPT-5.4 83.0% (Mar 2026) → GPT-5.5 84.9% (Apr 2026) — past the 50% parity line.
'One notable omission from OpenAI's Astra launch materials is GDPval, the company's own benchmark for measuring performance on economically valuable, real-world work.' — VentureBeat, Sep 3, 2026
OpenAI's own GDPval leaderboard page now reads: 'The OpenAI-hosted GDPval leaderboard is no longer active.'

Independent GDPval-AA v2.1 (Artificial Analysis): Claude Opus 5.5 leads at 1867 Elo, ahead of Claude Sonnet 5.5 (1840); GPT-6 Astra (max) scores 1542. The best Elo rose from 920 (GPT-5, Aug 2025) to 1867 (Claude Opus 5.5, Sep 2026).
